note: A strip of seven street pieces, not a plate: four paving surfaces and three props, each drawn at whatever size and aspect it wants, separated by wide gutters. It loads as an auto-strip - the game finds the frames by alpha at load and a tile pins the frame index it resolves to - so order IS the address here and moving a piece renames every piece after it. The raw art arrived RGB and opaque; its alpha was keyed in by art-source/tilesets/key_background.py, per band, with the three props keyed at a much lower threshold than the pavers because their own ironwork is drawn inside the range the pavers call background. The ids below are live: urban.mapping.json selects urban3.street-square, and TileManifest and GroundRenderSystem name urban3.sidewalk and urban3.sidewalk-corner directly. Re-exporting is safe as long as the seven frames keep this order. The atlas has derived urban-tileset-3_height.png and _normal.png beside it, sampled at the same pixels; re-run 'gradlew.bat :asset-pipeline:deriveTileMaps' after any export or they read the relief of the sheet they replaced.
